title: BARK: A fully Bayesian tree kernel for black-box optimization
contribution: Fully Bayesian tree-kernel GP for BO that samples forest structures by MCMC with BART-style priors while marginalising leaf values, and optimises the integrated UCB globally as a mixed-integer program over the tree encodings (read: arXiv v2).
problem_entry: Tree surrogates lack uncertainty for BO; prior tree kernels (incl. the group's LeafGP) use a two-step fit, 'not principled and hence potentially sub-optimal', or a single MAP tree that overfits (pp. 1, 4).
key_idea: BART's implicit GP: marginalise leaf values so each MCMC sample of tree structure is a GP; remove BART's k parameter, sample splits uniformly over the domain region reaching a node, and optimise the sample-averaged UCB as a MIP with an SOC variance constraint (pp. 3-6, 28).
assumptions: Gaussian noise with inverse-gamma prior; m = 50 trees, depth prior (0.95, 2), sigma0^2 = 1 on standardised outputs; discontinuous non-stationary prior violates regret-bound assumptions; MIP solved to a 10% gap in 100 s (pp. 4-6, 16, 26-27).
proof_devices: low-rank Woodbury and matrix-determinant-lemma updates per tree proposal, O(N^2 L_t) (p. 5)
Metropolis-Hastings ratio: split-rule probabilities cancel, acceptance independent of split distribution (p. 22)
softplus-transformed noise random walk with Jacobian correction (pp. 22-23)
integrated UCB convex in mu and sigma; variance equality relaxed to SOC inequality (pp. 6, 28)
reported failed regret-bound routes (Srinivas-type, bandit, combinatorial semi-bandit) (pp. 23-24)
Laplace-kernel limit theorem under Poisson depth, then 'chopping process' derivation showing the approximation fails for the true depth prior (pp. 24-26)
experiments: UCI regression vs BART (Table 1 p. 8); 4 mixed synthetic + 4 applied BO benchmarks, 20 runs median/IQR, 100 iterations, baselines BART (wall-clock-matched grid), GP-RBF, LeafGP, SMAC, Entmoot, BARKPrior ablation; MAX finite-candidate materials task; failure case DiscreteRosenbrock; wall-time and sensitivity studies (pp. 7-9, 16-23).
positioning: Corrects the group's own LeafGP and Entmoot, uses Misic 2020 / Thebelt 2022a MIP encodings, builds on BART (Chipman 2010) and Linero 2017; 14-method comparison table (pp. 2, 6, 15).
writing: Summary figure then three bulleted contributions and a roadmap (p. 2); method explained term by term as differences from BART (pp. 4-5); named failure case and a 'most significant limitation' subsection in the main text (pp. 7, 9).
limits_future: Wall time ~50 s fit + up to 100 s acquisition (p. 9); O(N^3) training, 951.91 s per 1000 samples at n = 400 (p. 19); no regret bound (pp. 23-26); recommend other methods when evaluations are cheap (pp. 9, 20).

method_links.note: Tree-kernel surrogate encoded as binary constraints; integrated UCB optimised globally as a MIP (step 8); BASF co-authors and funding.
Re-grades the group's 2022 LeafGP as not principled; BARKPrior and MAX benchmark separate optimiser gain from inference gain.
BO-community benchmarking: 20 seeds median/IQR, baseline budget matched to wall clock, losses and failure case reported; no answer re-check and MIP stopped at 10% gap.
Only the parameter-hygiene steps: BART's k removed, defaults shown largely insensitive by an (alpha, beta) grid, 16-sample setting labelled a compromise; no two-extreme family.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Appendix I records the regret-bound arguments tried (Srinivas-type, bandit, semi-bandit) and a derivation showing the Laplace-kernel approximation fails for the BART/BARK depth prior.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: retrospective pool-based BO on an existing experimental dataset
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: MAX-phase benchmark over 403 known compounds used as a finite candidate set, ablating acquisition optimisation.

transferable: Marginalise leaf values analytically so each MCMC sample of a tree ensemble is a GP usable by standard acquisition functions (pp. 3, 5).
Low-rank Woodbury and determinant-lemma updates for per-tree MCMC proposals in a forest kernel (p. 5).
Optimise an integrated UCB over tree kernels as one MIP with the variance relaxed to an SOC inequality (p. 28).
Match a non-optimisable baseline's grid size to your method's wall-clock time and state it (p. 17).
Add a prior-only ablation of your own method to separate optimiser gain from inference gain (p. 8).
State the evaluation-cost regime (minutes, money) in which the method pays off beside the timing plot (p. 9).
coauthors: Toby Boyne, Jose Pablo Folch, Robert Matthew Lee (BASF), Behrang Shafei (BASF); Misener last author

quotes.text: While this heuristic gives good results in a variety of benchmarks, it is not principled and hence potentially sub-optimal.
We therefore recommend BARK for BO settings where the objective is expensive to evaluate, taking at least several minutes, or having a large associated financial cost.

title: Transfer learning Bayesian optimization for competitor DNA molecule design for use in diagnostic assays
contribution: Transfer-learning BO workflow for designing many similar competitor DNA molecules, showing on real PCR data that a latent-variable multi-output GP surrogate predicts best and needs fewer experiments than no-transfer and linear-transfer GPs (read: arXiv v2).
problem_entry: Many similar sequences, each needing expensive lab runs; optimising each from scratch discards information from previous tasks; concrete case: competitor DNA for a competitive-PCR diagnostic with a target rate and a drift threshold (p. 2).
key_idea: LVMOGP surrogate with distributional latent positions per competitor, target-vector EI times probability of feasibility for drift, and reduction of sequence design to base pairs and GC content (pp. 5-9).
assumptions: Gaussian noise, SE kernel and zero mean from a smoothness belief, standardised data, type-II ML with restarts (acknowledged to overfit at low data), latent dimension 10 in CV and 2 in BO (pp. 2, 27-31).
proof_devices: informal model nesting: LMC recovers MOGP, LVMOGP with linear latent kernel recovers LMC (p. 5)
LVMOGP variational lower bound written out (Eq. 21, p. 26)
ARD switch-off of unneeded latent dimensions explains insensitivity to latent dimension (p. 29)
experiments: Three designed synthetic regimes (uncorrelated, linear, offset; 5 datasets) (pp. 9-10); CV on 34 competitors / 592 points, 70 repeats (pp. 8, 10-11); retrospective BO from a candidate set, 2 scenarios x 2 first-point rules, 24 seeds, cumulative regret; 36 vs 49 and 37 vs 57 experiments (pp. 11-13); initial-surface sensitivity (pp. 34-36).
positioning: Against coregionalisation's linear-combination assumption and against latent-variable BO with point-estimate latents (Zhang 2020, Hutter 2021) (pp. 4-5); within biological BO and design-build-test-learn automation (pp. 1-2, 16).
writing: Workflow figure first, toy figure for model mechanics, results as CV then single-objective then penalised BO; hedged 'we believe', 'may be due to' (pp. 2-3, 6, 10, 13, 16); written by the first author (p. 35).
limits_future: Seed variance from hard hyperparameter optimisation, poor high-dimensional scaling, retrospective rather than closed-loop validation; future: better hyperparameter fitting, lab-automation pipelines, other function priors (pp. 11, 15-16).

method_links.note: Surrogate judged first by CV, then inside the full BO loop with two scenarios and two start rules; ranking depends on the start rule.
Retrospective design stated openly, tolerance tied to measurement error, losses reported; but seed counts (24 vs 25) and the averaging rule for failed runs differ between sections.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: retrospective pool-based BO on an existing experimental dataset
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Closed-loop BO infeasible for cost, so BO restricted to already measured candidates; centre-point start as fair control.

transferable: Replace a combinatorial biological design space by a few continuous descriptors (length, GC content) and let a design tool realise each choice (pp. 8-9).
Combine target-distance EI with a probability-of-feasibility factor for 'hit a target, keep a nuisance below a threshold' (p. 7).
Include a no-correlation synthetic case to measure negative transfer (p. 9).
Run retrospective BO over the measured candidate set when the closed loop is unaffordable, and say so (p. 11).
Control first-point advantage with a common centre start for all models (p. 12).
Report experiments-to-best within the lab's measurement tolerance and convert to experiments saved (p. 13).
coauthors: Ruby Sedgwick, John P. Goertz, Molly M. Stevens, Mark van der Wilk; Misener co-supervised the ML aspects (p. 35)

quotes.text: Rather than tackling the difficult combinatorial problem of optimizing the sequence directly, we reduce the problem to two key input variables
However, due to the cost of experiments, this was infeasible. Instead, we performed retrospective Bayesian optimization using the existing competitive DNA amplification dataset.

title: System-aware neural ODE processes for few-shot Bayesian optimization
contribution: SANODEP, a meta-learned neural ODE process conditioned on several trajectories, plus a model-agnostic two-stage BO framework for choosing initial conditions and measurement times under a minimum measurement delay, with a proposition halving the batch-size search range (read: arXiv v2).
problem_entry: Optimise initial conditions and termination time of an unknown ODE system where switching initial conditions is costly and measurements come with a delay; GP kernels miss dynamics and Bayesian ODE models are slow (pp. 1, 3, 6).
key_idea: Pool context points from many trajectories, each augmented with its initial condition, into a system latent; train with a Bernoulli mix of forecasting and interpolation; optimise with a two-stage batch BO under t_i - t_{i-1} >= Delta t (pp. 4-6, 20).
assumptions: Lipschitz f drawn from a known stochastic family F (parametric kinetic models in practice), fixed known delay, known aggregation g; Section 7 varies prior strength from known kinetic form to a GP vector-field prior (pp. 3-7, 9-10, 19-20).
proof_devices: Proposition 1: batch-size range reduced to {ceil(Nmax/2), ..., Nmax} for set-inclusion-monotone expected-utility acquisitions such as qEHVI (p. 6)
Lemma C.1 and Corollary C.1.1 (expectation preserves monotonicity) plus a gap-insertion argument (p. 19)
ELBO derivation for the bi-scenario loss (p. 17)
chain-rule argument for smooth activations to keep gradients in t and x0 (pp. 15-16)
experiments: Six ODE systems; MSE/NLL vs number of context trajectories on 10^4 test systems (GP on 5,000 trajectories), 5 training seeds (pp. 7-8, 21); few-shot BO with 1 + 10 trajectories, 10 seeds, hypervolume vs scaled time (pp. 8-9, 22); timing table (p. 23).
positioning: Extends NODEP and Neural Processes; distinguishes from discrete-time or regular-grid meta-learned dynamics and from GP drop-in few-shot BO surrogates; relates to process-constrained BO and the group's SnAKe / transition-constrained BO (pp. 2-3, 6-7).
writing: Four numbered contributions (p. 2); results under question headings (pp. 8-9); dedicated limitations paragraph (p. 10); several typographical slips in the arXiv text (p. 9).
limits_future: NP underfitting trades few-shot ability against fit; without the kinetic form the model 'cannot be used out of the box'; oscillatory systems hard; PI training needed parameter clipping; future: more adaptable conditional distributions, meta-learned parameter estimation (pp. 10, 26-27).

method_links.note: Structure exploited in the acquisition problem (set-inclusion monotonicity cuts the integer range) and, when known, the kinetic form built into the model.
One model-agnostic BO framework in which GP, NP, NODEP and SANODEP are switchable surrogates; not a partner's trained model.
Spectrum of prior strength (known kinetic form to GP vector-field prior) with a flexibility-fit trade-off, labelled preliminary, no proven ordering.
Cost-driven GP subsampling and an impossible comparison named, timings reported; only 10 BO seeds and small mismatches between Tables 1 and 2.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: experimental-protocol constraints as first-class BO constraints
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Measurement delay Delta t and costly initial-condition switches define the decision problem; links to the group's SnAKe and transition-constrained BO.

transferable: Prove set-inclusion monotonicity of an expected-utility batch acquisition to cut the batch-size variable's range (pp. 6, 19).
Augment each context element with its run identifier (initial condition) before mean pooling (pp. 4-5).
Train a meta-learned surrogate on a Bernoulli mix of the prediction tasks the optimiser will need (p. 5).
Check surrogate differentiability w.r.t. decision variables and swap ReLU for smooth activations before gradient-based acquisition optimisation (pp. 15-16).
Report surrogate error against the number of context trajectories to show where meta-learning helps and where a GP overtakes (p. 8).
coauthors: Jixiang Qing, Becky D Langdon, Robert M Lee (BASF), Behrang Shafei (BASF), Mark van der Wilk, Calvin Tsay; Misener last author

quotes.text: A meta-learned BO method specifically for dynamical systems is, to our best of knowledge, not revealed yet.

SANODEP still faces a trade-off between model fitting and prior flexibility, indicating that it cannot be used out of the box as a generic probabilistic model to optimize arbitrary dynamical system without knowing its kinetic form.
